page: Microsoft Azure E4s_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor running at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz. Compute resources include 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. System memory totals 32.0 GB, providing an 8.0 GB RAM-to-vCPU ratio. Cache architecture features 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of shared L3 cache. The CPU incorporates instruction sets including AVX-512 extensions (F and VNNI) as well as hardware cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The server includes no bundled local storage and operates with zero discrete GPUs and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks place the instance in mid-tier single-threaded standing and lower-tier multi-threaded throughput, aligned with its 4-vCPU scale. Single-core performance registers a score of 1664.0 in Geekbench and 1897.19 in stress-ng. In multi-core scenarios, Geekbench records 3527.0 and stress-ng measures 3873.38, reflecting the physical limitation of two cores. PassMark metrics indicate a total CPU score of 5897.5 and a memory score of 2323.52. Large-block memory bandwidth benchmarks produce 29.84 GB/sec for uncached reads and 25.22 GB/sec for writes. In application-focused metrics, Redis SET throughput reaches 4.03 million operations per second, while static web serving delivers 6.53 GB/sec throughput.

From an infrastructure and resource efficiency perspective, the E4s_v5 delivers a high memory-per-core allocation without the hardware overhead of local disks or dedicated GPUs. Storage operations rely entirely on attached network volumes. This configuration suits workloads demanding substantial memory buffers but modest compute parallelism, such as medium-sized relational databases, Redis caching layers, enterprise backend services, and lightweight ETL pipelines.
